title: Ligaments of the hip joint and pelvis (anterior)
attribution: 3D anatomy from Z-Anatomy, built on BodyParts3D (CC BY-SA). Rendered in Blender; surface detail added with an image model.

rows: Attachments
Anterior inferior iliac spine and the rim of the acetabulum to the lower part of the intertrochanteric line of the femur.
Function
With the transverse part it forms a Y-shaped ligament across the front of the hip. It limits extension of the hip, which lets a person stand with little muscular effort.
Attachments
Anterior inferior iliac spine and the rim of the acetabulum to the upper part of the intertrochanteric line of the femur.
Function
With the descending part it forms a Y-shaped ligament across the front of the hip. It limits extension and lateral rotation of the hip.
Attachments
Superior ramus of the pubis to the lower part of the neck of the femur, blending with the joint capsule.
Function
Limits abduction and extension of the hip.
Attachments
Front of the sacrum to the adjacent part of the ilium.
Function
A thin sheet that strengthens the front of the sacroiliac joint.
Attachments
Transverse process of L5 to the posterior part of the iliac crest.
Function
Anchors L5 to the pelvis and keeps it from sliding forward on the sacrum.
Attachments
Lateral margin of the sacrum and coccyx to the ischial spine.
Function
Turns the greater sciatic notch into the greater sciatic foramen and separates it from the lesser sciatic foramen. It resists upward tilting of the lower sacrum.
hy: The pudendal nerve leaves the pelvis through the greater sciatic foramen, hooks around the ischial spine and this ligament, and enters the perineum through the lesser sciatic foramen.

rows: Attachments
Posterior ilium, lateral sacrum and coccyx to the ischial tuberosity.
Function
With the sacrospinous ligament it turns the sciatic notches into foramina and resists upward tilting of the lower sacrum under the weight of the trunk.
Attachments
Margins of the obturator foramen, closing it except for the obturator canal at the top.
Function
Gives origin to obturator internus and obturator externus. The obturator nerve and vessels leave the pelvis through the obturator canal.
Attachments
Runs between the two pubic bones along the top of the pubic symphysis.
Function
Strengthens the pubic symphysis from above.
Attachments
Arches between the inferior rami of the two pubic bones, below the pubic symphysis.
Function
Strengthens the pubic symphysis from below and forms the top of the pubic arch.
Location
Plate of fibrocartilage that fills the pubic symphysis, between the bodies of the two pubic bones.
Function
Joins the two pubic bones at the front of the pelvic ring and allows a little movement; the superior and inferior pubic ligaments strengthen it. The joint loosens in late pregnancy.
